The final guidelines specify three assurance levels for authentication and define requirements for credential issuance, binding, and lifecycle management. At the highest level, authentication requires a hardware-protected cryptographic key and multi-factor verification; knowledge-based questions are no longer permitted as a sole factor. Session management requirements were tightened — reauthentication is required after 12 hours at the second level and 30 minutes of inactivity at the third. Federation protocols must use signed assertions with audience restriction, and relying parties must verify them against published keys. The document also addresses privacy, directing agencies to minimize collection of attributes and to conduct a privacy risk assessment. Compared with the draft, comments led to revised language on biometric performance thresholds and clearer guidance on account recovery.
